messages:
Micah: Quick follow-up on the packaging RFC — when we say 'retire a package' in onprem/offline installs, do we mean hard-delete from disk or mark it inactive (tombstone)? If hard-delete, how do we guarantee offline rollbacks for pods/operators that pinned older manifests? :thinking:
Anya: My vote is for tombstone + lease rather than immediate deletion. In airgapped installs you can't rely on re-downloading, so a soft-retire lets operators still validate and roll back if needed.
Sam: Tombstone sounds safer, but we need clear GC rules. Operators hate surprises when disk fills. We should define: max_retire_age, eviction_policy (LRU by last-activation), and an admin-trigger to force prune.
Kevin: Agree. Also propose an activation hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping when canaries toggle: add manifest field `activation_hysteresis_seconds` + `retire_after_seconds`. Example manifest fragment: ```
{
  "package": "model-v2.1.0",
  "activation_hysteresis_seconds": 3600,
  "retire_after_seconds": 86400,
  "pin_id": "team-A-prod"
}
```
That way a package that briefly becomes inactive won't be eligible for GC until the hysteresis passes.
Micah: Nice. How does that interact with pinned versions? If a customer pins `model-v2.0.7` and it's tombstoned, should we prevent GC regardless of retire timers?
Anya: Pins must win. If `pin_id` exists in any active rollout config or is referenced by an admin, GC should skip. We surface pins in the operator UI and API: `GET /local-store?pinned=true`.
Sam: Edge-case: operator transfer between clusters (seed handoff). If target cluster doesn't have the tombstoned blobs, we need a deterministic error rather than silent fallback. Suggest: on activation, validate that all blobs exist locally or at the seed. If not, fail activation with clear error code `ERR_MISSING_BLOB` and instructions.
Kevin: For disk pressure cases we can add an emergency-evict policy: allow auto-evict of non-pinned tombstones oldest-first, but require a 24h alert and a signed admin override to actually delete in airgap. Put hooks in the operator UI and include a `dry_run=true` option.
Micah: Sounds good. We also need an audit trail: tombstone/create/delete events should be logged to the control plane (or local audit log for private deployments). Include fields: actor, reason, source (operator/admin/auto-gc), and checksum of removed blobs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC updated: onprem-packaging-retire-controls.md (patch 3). Review requested from @Anya @Kevin @Sam.
Anya: I can draft the GC operator API and the admin UI flows tomorrow.
Sam: I'll write the failure-mode tests: missing blob activation, pin-protection, and emergency-evict.
Kevin: I'll add the hysteresis + manifest validation to the manifest parser and runtime checks.
Micah: Ok action items: (1) Anya: API + UI draft, (2) Sam: tests / runbook, (3) Kevin: runtime + manifest change, (4) Ops: add audit fields to local log format. Follow up in this thread when drafts exist. :+1:
Micah: One more: add a short CLI helper `rw-pack gc --simulate` to preview what would be deleted on a node. That should print tombstone age, pins, and backrefs.
Anya: Good idea — helps admins in airgap where debugging is manual.
Sam: ack.
Micah: Thanks all — locking this thread for notes, will reference in RFC followup doc.
